decision: TWO ITEMS. (A) SECOND ENFORCEMENT BYPASS: report, decline to self-remediate, and declare it covered by my D006 substance-binding. The designer found, and I verified on a scratch copy that I then deleted, that falsify/cli.py::required_level runs its manipulation checks inside 'for c in spec.get(cells, [])' (cli.py:154,165) and computes n_trials as len(cells) * len(seeds) (cli.py:170), so a spec WITH NO cells KEY has BOTH the preregistered-condition check AND the trial-budget check vacuous. My scratch spec - no cells, primary_outcome 'BRAND NEW OUTCOME never preregistered', auditor_mode 'real' - returned required_level 1, 'inside preregistered condition space, mandated model, within level-1 budget'. This is STRICTLY WORSE than the D006 rename bypass because 0 cells times any seeds is 0 trials, so any run size also passes, and commit be90931's allowlists only validate keys within cells that already exist. It is LIVE, not hypothetical: a cell-less standalone calibration harness is exactly the shape of the designer's own candidate A. Logged for the human at 12:33:49 with a suggested repair. I am NOT patching it. I declare, on substance, that any cell-less new-instrument spec with a new primary outcome is LEVEL 2 for me regardless of what the CLI returns. (B) DISCHARGE THE D008 CONCERNS. (B1) I WITHDRAW THE LITERATURE WARRANT for the error-correlation prior. In D008 I wrote that it is 'independently supported by the literature's reading of Huang et al. 2023 and Panickssery et al. 2024'. The reviewer is right that neither source addresses whether four role-differentiated instances err TOGETHER: Huang 2023 is single-model self-correction (candidates.md:70) and Panickssery 2024 is self-preference assigned to H4 (candidates.md:76). My provenance labelling was accurate and section J compliant, but the RELEVANCE was not, and borrowing them gave the prior an 'independently supported' badge it had not earned - which, as the reviewer puts it, is exactly how a retracted finding keeps doing its old work under a new label. My item (1) was undone one field below it. (B2) The prior now rests ONLY on verified architectural grounds: one model at one temperature, four roles reading the same prompt-certified sentence from one shared log (falsify/org.py:83-95), with planner and executor coupled by EDGE_CASE_POLICY section F. That is an argument about OUR architecture, which is the right basis for OUR spending. (B3) THE PRIOR IS SEALED: it is NOT updated by C-005 or by any exp001_pilot trial; it is moved only by a measured non-zero route-intention disagreement rate in a design where roles do NOT share a certified answer; and it may license DECLINING to spend, never spending, and never a registration or a status change. (B4) NON-INDEPENDENCE CLAUSE added: C-005 is one of the 20 trials already counted in the 20/20 and the 0/80, so it adds NO independent evidential weight and is illustration only - citing it beside the zero without this note is soft double-counting. (B5) I accept the reviewer's two self-corrections and have forwarded both to the human as engineer requests: cmd_decide attaches code_hashes only inside 'if a.spec:' so spec-less decisions cannot carry one, and decision records have no amended_by field so I will NOT hand-edit D005 or D007. (B6) results/exp001_pilot_reaggregation_memo.md:161 still ranks C-005 'the single most important qualitative point in the file' - the same emphasis-ranking I retracted; the statistician, not I, corrects that.
reason: On (A): this is the second bypass in one loop and the first one's fix did not cover it, which is itself the finding. The D006 lesson was that an automated authority floor can report compliance while being circumventable; the lesson here is stronger, because a targeted repair closed the specific hole that was reported and left a wider one open in the same function. That is an argument for failing closed on structure rather than enumerating known evasions, and it is why I am not relaxing the substance-binding now that two separate CLI defects have been found. I verified it myself rather than relaying the designer, per D010, and I cleaned up the scratch spec. I note the uncomfortable coincidence that the bypass is shaped exactly like the design I am being asked to approve, which is a reason to be more careful about that approval, not less. On (B): the reviewer's finding is the subtlest of the loop and it caught me doing something I had just finished condemning. D008 retracted a mechanism claim from n=1 and then, one field lower, propped up the surviving 'prior' with two citations that do not bear on inter-agent error correlation at all. The citations were honestly labelled as abstract-only and ADJACENT, so this was not a provenance failure; it was a relevance failure, which is harder to see and does the same work. The honest warrant was available and free, and it is stronger for our purposes because it is a claim about our own architecture rather than a borrowed generalization: four roles reading one certified sentence from one shared log, same model, same temperature, planner and executor coupled by policy. Sealing the prior is the part that makes the retraction stick - without an explicit statement of what can and cannot move it, and of what it may and may not license, 'prior' is just a label that lets the retracted claim keep operating. I am stating the seal rather than trusting myself to remember it.
alternatives_rejected: Patch the cell-less bypass myself, since it is a two-line fail-closed change and the first fix demonstrably missed it: REJECTED on the same grounds as D006, and more firmly now. The temptation is stronger because the hole is wider and because I can see the repair, which is exactly when the separation of duty matters most; and the reviewer's own correction to my D006 reasoning stands, so I rest this on separation of duty and zero-cost delegation rather than on the false 'weaker instrument' claim. | Treat the cell-less bypass as closed because I have self-bound to substance: REJECTED. My self-binding constrains ME; it does nothing about any other agent, any future loop, or an automated run, and the CLI remains the artifact AUTHORITY.md points at as the enforcement mechanism. | Approve the designer's recommended exp010 now: REJECTED AS PREMATURE on two independent grounds. The skeptic has not yet reported on the exp009 readout and is next in the human's mandated sequence; and the designer's memo was written WITHOUT the exp009 result, which it says explicitly, so its ranking has not been tested against the livelock finding or against the missing honest-report affordance. I will not approve a level-2 experiment on a ranking that predates the loop's most consequential measurement. | Keep the Huang and Panickssery citations with a hedge: REJECTED, a hedge does not fix a relevance failure, and the architectural warrant is both sufficient and more apt. | Retract the error-correlation prior entirely: REJECTED as over-correction for the second time; the architectural grounds are verified and real, and the correct remedy is to narrow and seal the prior rather than discard a sound consideration. | Hand-edit D005 and D007 to mark the retracted text: REJECTED, records are append-only and the reviewer explicitly told me to request an amended_by field instead of editing prior decisions.
